label: Elected title
summary: The title whose election this elector takes part in, as shown in the succession election window.
details: Vanilla goes on from it to the title's player nominee (GetPlayerNominee) in the vote breakdown: "Your candidate, …" and "Will vote for … if their score is greater than …". That it is the title being elected rests on its name and those texts. The game documents no return type.

label: Vote strength
summary: A whole number: how much weight this elector's vote carries in the election.
details: Vanilla shows it as a value in the shared succession election widgets. That it is the vote's weight rests on its name and that use.

label: Vote strength breakdown
summary: A text listing what makes up this elector's vote strength.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip in the shared succession election widgets, next to the vote strength (GetVoteStrength). The content rests on its name and that use.

label: Votes for player's candidate
summary: Yes or no: whether this elector votes for the player's candidate.
details: Vanilla shows a widget only when the title has a player nominee and this is no: the elector's vote is not (yet) for the player's candidate. The meaning rests on its name and that use.

label: Elector itself
summary: A function on an elector of the succession election window that, going by its name, hands back the elector itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access vote itself
summary: A function on an elector's vote in a succession election that, going by its name, hands back the vote itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Voted candidate
summary: Going by its name, the candidate this elector's vote goes to.
details: Vanilla never names it as SuccessionElectionElectorVote.GetCandidate. The rank text goes from SuccessionElectionElector.GetElectorCandidate to GetCandidate and hands it to SuccessionElectionWindow.GetCandidateFromCharacter, so it likely gives a character, but which type GetElectorCandidate returns is not shown: a hint only. The game documents no return type.

label: Vote score
summary: A whole number: the score this vote gives its candidate.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Score: …" in the election window, formatted as a signed number (the game's |+ format). What the score is made of is not shown; the meaning rests on its name and that text.

label: Vote itself
summary: A function on an elector's vote in a succession election that, going by its name, hands back the vote itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access election window
summary: A function on the succession election window (the window showing an elective title's candidates and electors) that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close election window
summary: Closes the succession election window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button in the title election window (window_title_election.gui). It returns nothing.

label: Candidate entry of character
summary: The election window's candidate entry for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes Character.Self to get the entry for a character shown in the window, and in the rank text goes on to the entry's GetElectionRank. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose candidate entry is wanted.

label: Candidates
summary: The list of candidates in the succession election window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the candidate list and counts it in the heading "Candidates (…)". The game documents no return type.

label: Who can be candidate
summary: A text naming which group of characters can be candidates in this election.
details: Vanilla shows it in the rules part of the election window as "Candidates: …", with GetCandidatesGroupingTooltip as its tooltip. That it names the group rests on its name and that text.

label: Candidate group tooltip
summary: The tooltip text explaining the group of characters that can be candidates.
details: Vanilla shows it on the "Candidates: …" line in the rules part of the election window. The content rests on its name and that use.

label: Elector entry of character
summary: The election window's elector entry for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes Character.Self inside the elector list, after taking the character of a list item. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose elector entry is wanted.

label: Elector vote strength breakdown
summary: A text listing what makes up the given character's vote strength in this election.
details: Vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer) and shows it as a tooltip next to the player's vote strength. The content rests on its name and that use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The elector whose vote strength is broken down.

label: Electors
summary: The list of electors (the characters who vote) in the succession election window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the elector list and counts it in the heading "Electors (…)". The game documents no return type.

label: Who votes
summary: A text naming which group of characters are electors in this election.
details: Vanilla shows it in the rules part of the election window as "Electors: …", with GetElectorsGroupingTooltip as its tooltip. That it names the group rests on its name and that text.

label: Elector group tooltip
summary: The tooltip text explaining the group of characters that are electors.
details: Vanilla shows it on the "Electors: …" line in the rules part of the election window. The content rests on its name and that use.

label: Relevance breakdown
summary: A value breakdown of the given candidate's relevance in the election, for a debug tooltip.
details: Vanilla passes Character.Self and shows it in a breakdown tooltip on the "Relevance: …" line, which is visible only in debug mode. What relevance means is not documented. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The candidate whose relevance is broken down.

label: Succession law
summary: The succession law used by the election shown in the window.
details: It leads on to the law itself (type Law). Vanilla shows its name as "Succession Law: …" and uses it in the princely elective electors tooltip.

label: Elected title
summary: The title whose succession election the window shows.
details: Vanilla goes on from it to the title's holder and to its custom texts in the princely elective electors tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Character's vote strength
summary: A whole number: how much weight the given character's vote carries in this election.
details: Vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer) and shows the value in the election window, with GetElectorVoteStrengthBreakdown as its tooltip. That it is the vote's weight rests on its name and that use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The elector whose vote strength is wanted.

label: Election window itself
summary: A function on the succession election window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access candidate entry
summary: A function on a candidate entry of the succession election window that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Candidate
summary: The candidate character this entry of the election window stands for.
details: Vanilla shows the candidate's name in the score tooltip: "Electors voting for …". The game documents no return type.

label: Election rank
summary: A whole number: the candidate's place in the election, 1 being the one currently ahead.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Rank: …" and checks whether it equals 1 to show a winning or losing stance and to show a widget only for the leading candidate.

label: Electors voting for candidate
summary: The list of electors who vote for this candidate.
details: Vanilla counts it in "… Electors vote for him/her" and shows a part of the window only when the list has items. The game documents no return type.

label: Candidate relevance
summary: A whole number: the candidate's relevance in the election, a debug value.
details: Vanilla shows it only in debug mode as "Relevance: …", with SuccessionElectionWindow.GetRelevanceBreakdown as its tooltip. What relevance stands for is not documented.

label: Candidate score
summary: A whole number, never negative: the candidate's total score in the election.
details: Vanilla's tooltip calls it the total score of the candidate and says the candidate with the highest score inherits the title on succession. The window hides it when it is 0.

label: Votes in favor
summary: A text listing the electors who vote for this candidate.
details: Vanilla shows it in the score tooltip after "Electors voting for …:".

label: Candidate entry itself
summary: A function on a candidate entry of the succession election window that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access elector itself
summary: A function on a succession elector that, going by its name, hands back the elector itself.
details: Vanilla never names this type. PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Elector character
summary: Going by its name, the character who is this succession elector.
details: Vanilla never names this type; GetCharacter after other types (such as CouncilWindow.GetCharacter) is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Vote strength
summary: A whole number that, going by its name, is how much weight this elector's vote carries.
details: Vanilla never names this type. SuccessionElectionElector.GetVoteStrength and SuccessionElectionWindow.GetVoteStrength are other types: a hint only.

label: Elector itself
summary: A function on a succession elector that, going by its name, hands back the elector itself.
details: Vanilla never names this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access succession window
summary: A function on the succession window (shown when the player character dies or is deposed) that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Can choose new character
summary: Yes or no: whether the player may switch to another character from the succession window.
details: Vanilla shows the "Enter Observer Mode" and "Choose new Character" buttons only when the player has no heir to continue as and this is yes. The meaning rests on its name and those buttons.

label: Choose new character
summary: Lets the player pick a new character to play after their line ended.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Choose new Character" button, shown only when there is no heir to continue as. What happens next (the character selection) rests on the button's text. It returns nothing.

label: Close succession window
summary: Closes the succession window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the close button of the lineage window and when an animation of the succession window finishes. It returns nothing.

label: Confirm new destiny
summary: Confirms the character chosen under "Choose a New Destiny", so the player goes on as that character.
details: A new destiny lets the player play another character of their dynasty who is not their heir. Vanilla has two confirm buttons, one for a chosen character and one for a random pick (IsSelectedDestinyCharacterRandom). That the player then plays as them rests on the name and the button texts. It returns nothing.

label: Continue-as character
summary: The character the player will go on playing as after the succession.
details: Vanilla names this character on the close button: "Continue as …". The game documents no return type.

label: Previous character
summary: The character the player was playing before the succession, usually the one who died.
details: Vanilla uses it for the game-over texts when the end date is reached (its custom texts on duration, splendor and notable achievements), checks whether this character is still alive (a deposed ruler) and goes on to their dynasty in the lineage window. The game documents no return type.

label: Previous character's legacy
summary: The legacy entry (the record in the player's lineage) of the character the player just stopped playing.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for one part of the succession window. What the entry holds rests on its name and that use. The game documents no return type.

label: Previous character text
summary: A text about the character the player just stopped playing, shown in the succession window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the succession window's character part, above the heir's text (GetHeirDesc). The content rests on its name and that use.

label: End date of play
summary: The date the player's run ended, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows its year after the start year in the dynasty info: "start year - end year". The game documents no return type.

label: Exit button text
summary: The text of the menu button of the succession window.
details: Vanilla shows it on the menu button, visible only when there is no heir to continue as; clicking it calls GoToMenu.

label: Exit button tooltip
summary: The tooltip of the menu button of the succession window.
details: Vanilla shows it on the menu button that calls GoToMenu.

label: Favorite child
summary: Going by its name, the favorite child of the player's previous character.
details: Vanilla compares it with each shown character and marks the match with the favorite child icon ("Is your favorite child"). Whose favorite child it is rests on its name and that use. The game documents no return type.

label: Succession window heading
summary: The heading text of the succession window.
details: Vanilla shows it at the top while the window shows a succession (IsSuccession). The game's headings for this window include "You have died", "You have been deposed", "Game Over" and "The End"; which one this returns in which case is not shown.

label: Heir text
summary: A text about the heir the player goes on as, shown in the succession window.
details: Vanilla shows it below the previous character's text (GetDeadDesc). The content rests on its name and that use.

label: Inherited titles
summary: The list of titles the player's heir inherits.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the inherited titles list and shows that part only when the list has items. The game documents no return type.

label: Lineage entries
summary: The list of earlier characters in the player's lineage (the line of characters played so far).
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for a row of entries in the lineage window and the succession window, and adds a spacer when the list is not empty. That these are the characters played before rests on its name and those uses. The game documents no return type.

label: Lost titles
summary: The list of titles lost on succession, grouped by who receives them.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the lost titles part, shown when the player expands it (ShowLostTitles). Each item names an heir (SuccessionEventWindowLostTitlesItem.GetHeir) and their titles. The game documents no return type.

label: Destiny characters
summary: The list of dynasty characters the player can pick under "Choose a New Destiny".
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the main character list of the new destiny part. That these are the main choices, beside the random ones (GetRandomDestinyCharacters), rests on its name. The game documents no return type.

label: Number of lost titles
summary: A whole number: how many titles were lost on succession.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Titles lost on Succession: …" and adds a warning icon when it is not 0.

label: Characters played
summary: A whole number: how many members of the dynasty the player has played.
details: Vanilla shows it in the dynasty info as "… Members (… Played)".

label: Time played
summary: A text giving how long the player's line lasted.
details: Vanilla uses it in "With no player heir, your line has died out after …".

label: Player heir
summary: The player heir: the character the player goes on as after the succession, if there is one.
details: Vanilla checks whether it is valid: with an heir it shows the lineage of that heir; without one it shows the observer, new character and exit buttons instead. The game documents no return type.

label: Player heir's legacy
summary: The legacy entry (the record in the player's lineage) of the player heir.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the current lineage part of the lineage window and for parts of the succession window. What the entry holds rests on its name and those uses. The game documents no return type.

label: Primary heir
summary: Going by its name, the primary heir of the player's previous character.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents no return type.

label: Random destiny choices
summary: The list of options for a random new destiny.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the "Let Fate Decide" part, whose tooltip says a random character is chosen from one of several categories. That the items are those categories rests on that text. The game documents no return type.

label: Selected destiny
summary: The new destiny entry the player has currently selected.
details: Vanilla shows its type name on the button "Continue as …" and enables the confirm button only when the entry has a valid character (GetCharacter). The game documents no return type.

label: Start date of play
summary: The date the player's run began, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows its year before the end year in the dynasty info: "start year - end year". The game documents no return type.

label: Leave to menu
summary: Leaves the game for the menu from the succession window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the menu button, shown only when there is no heir to continue as; its text and tooltip come from GetExitName and GetExitTooltip. That it goes to the menu rests on its name. It returns nothing.

label: Enter observer mode
summary: Puts the player into observer mode (watching the game without a character) from the succession window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Enter Observer Mode" button, shown only when there is no heir and the player may change character. It returns nothing.

label: Has lost titles
summary: Yes or no: whether any titles were lost on succession.
details: Vanilla shows the lost titles list only when this is yes and the list is expanded (ShowLostTitles).

label: Has destiny characters
summary: Yes or no that, going by its name, tells whether there are characters in the main new destiny list.
details: Vanilla never uses it; GetMainDestinyCharacters is the list it refers to by name.

label: Has random destiny options
summary: Yes or no: whether a random new destiny can be chosen.
details: Vanilla enables the "Select Random Destiny" button only when this is yes.

label: Has new destiny options
summary: Yes or no: whether there are dynasty characters the player could take up as a new destiny.
details: Vanilla enables the new destiny and "Return to your Dynasty" buttons only when this is yes; when it is no, the tooltip says there are no suitable dynasty characters.

label: End date reached
summary: Yes or no: whether the game's end date has been reached.
details: Vanilla switches parts of the succession window on it: the end date text ("The end date of the game has been reached.") instead of the usual death view.

label: Shows lineage
summary: Yes or no: whether the window is shown as the lineage view.
details: Vanilla shows the top lineage part (with the inherited titles) only when this is yes. The window also has IsSuccession for the succession view. The meaning rests on its name and that use.

label: Lineage tab open
summary: Yes or no: whether the lineage tab of the succession window is open.
details: Vanilla shows the lineage tab button as pressed while this is yes.

label: New destiny open
summary: Yes or no: whether the "Choose a New Destiny" part is open.
details: Vanilla lets clicks pass through the window's main part while this is no. ToggleSelectDestinyOpen opens and closes it.

label: Random destiny selected
summary: Yes or no: whether the selected new destiny is a random pick rather than a chosen character.
details: Vanilla shows one of two confirm buttons depending on it; both call ConfirmSelectDestinyCharacter.

label: Shows succession
summary: Yes or no: whether the window is shown as the succession view (after a death or deposition).
details: Vanilla shows the heading part and the bottom buttons only when this is yes. The window also has IsLineage for the lineage view. The meaning rests on its name and those uses.

label: Successor tab open
summary: Yes or no: whether the successor tab of the succession window is open.
details: Vanilla shows the successor tab button as pressed while this is yes.

label: Titles tab open
summary: Yes or no: whether the titles tab of the succession window is open.
details: Vanilla shows the titles tab button as pressed while this is yes.

label: Open lineage tab
summary: Opens the lineage tab of the succession window.
details: Vanilla calls it when the lineage tab button's animation finishes. It returns nothing.

label: Open successor tab
summary: Opens the successor tab of the succession window.
details: Vanilla calls it when the successor tab button's animation finishes. It returns nothing.

label: Open titles tab
summary: Opens the titles tab of the succession window.
details: Vanilla calls it when the titles tab button's animation finishes. It returns nothing.

label: Select destiny
summary: Selects the given entry as the player's new destiny, before it is confirmed.
details: Vanilla passes DestinyCharacter.Self when an entry of the new destiny lists is clicked; ConfirmSelectDestinyCharacter then confirms it. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The new destiny entry to select.
fields.values: a destiny entry, as in DestinyCharacter.Self

label: Succession window itself
summary: A function on the succession window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Lost titles expanded
summary: Yes or no: whether the lost titles list is expanded.
details: Vanilla sets the expand button's look from it and shows the list only when this is yes and there are lost titles (HasLostTitles). ToggleLostTitles switches it.

label: Expand lost titles
summary: Expands or collapses the list of titles lost on succession.
details: Vanilla calls it from the expand button beside "Titles lost on Succession". It returns nothing.

label: Toggle new destiny
summary: Opens or closes the "Choose a New Destiny" part of the succession window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the new destiny button, the "Return to your Dynasty" button and a button inside that part. It returns nothing.

label: Access lost titles entry
summary: A function on an entry of the succession window's lost titles list that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Heir of lost titles
summary: The character who receives the titles of this lost titles entry.
details: It leads to a character. Vanilla shows that character's name in the entry and uses them as the data for the entry's character part.

label: Lost titles
summary: The list of titles in this lost titles entry, the ones its heir receives.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for the titles shown in the entry. The game documents no return type.

label: Lost titles entry itself
summary: A function on an entry of the lost titles list that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Law group
summary: The law group whose law the window changes.
details: Vanilla goes on to GetLawGroup.GetName for the headings "Change …" and "Available …". The game documents no return type.

label: Access law change window
summary: A function on the succession law change window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close law change window
summary: Closes the succession law change window.
details: Vanilla calls it from buttons of that window. It returns nothing.

label: Appointment laws
summary: The list of appointment succession laws offered in the law change window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for one group of law buttons, shown only when the list has items. That they are appointment laws rests on its name. The game documents no return type.

label: House
summary: The dynasty house shown in the law change window.
details: Vanilla goes on to the house's current house unity stage and shows it only when the house is valid and has house unity. Whose house it is rests on its name and that use. The game documents no return type.

label: Line of succession
summary: Going by its name, the line of succession shown in the law change window.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Title.GetLineOfSuccession and MyRealmWindow.GetLineOfSuccession are other types and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Other laws
summary: The list of other laws offered in the law change window, outside the named groups.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for a grid of law buttons, shown only when the list has items. Which laws count as other rests on its name. The game documents no return type.

label: Partition laws
summary: The list of partition succession laws (laws that split titles among heirs) offered in the law change window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for one group of law buttons, shown only when the list has items. That they are partition laws rests on its name. The game documents no return type.

label: Powerful vassals
summary: The list of powerful vassals shown in the law change window.
details: Vanilla shows it under the window's powerful vassals heading. Powerful vassals are the ones who must approve some law changes (see GetSelectedLaw's ShouldBeApproved). The game documents no return type.

label: Selected law
summary: The law currently selected in the law change window.
details: It leads to an interface law (type GuiLaw). Vanilla shows its cost ("Cost: …") and cost description, and shows a part only when it has to be approved and the player's government does not deny powerful vassals.

label: Single heir laws
summary: The list of single heir succession laws offered in the law change window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data for one group of law buttons, shown only when the list has items. That they are single heir laws rests on its name. The game documents no return type.

label: Titles
summary: Going by its name, a list of titles in the law change window.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; CharacterWindow.GetTitles and others are other types and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Law change window itself
summary: A function on the succession law change window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access suggestion itself
summary: A function on a suggestion (an action the game proposes to the player) that, going by its name, hands back the suggestion itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Dismiss suggestion
summary: Dismisses the suggestion shown to the player.
details: Vanilla calls it on a right click on the suggestion button and from its small cancel button. It returns nothing.

label: Suggestion description
summary: Going by its name, the description text of the suggestion.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetDescription after other types is only a hint.

label: Suggestion label
summary: The text shown on the suggestion button.
details: Vanilla shows it as the button's text in the suggestion template.

label: Selection marker
summary: A text that, going by its name, marks the suggestion's selection.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Suggestion type
summary: Going by its name, the suggestion type (a definition in common/suggestions) this suggestion comes from.
details: Vanilla never uses it. Each suggestion type in common/suggestions can create several suggestions for different targets. The game documents no return type.

label: Suggestion tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the suggestion button.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip in the suggestion template.

label: Click suggestion
summary: Acts on the suggestion when the player clicks it.
details: Vanilla calls it on a left click on the suggestion button. The suggestion type's `effect` block is what runs when the player clicks a suggestion. It returns nothing.

label: Suggestion itself
summary: A function on a suggestion that, going by its name, hands back the suggestion itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access suggestion type
summary: A function on a suggestion type (a definition in common/suggestions) that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Suggestion type name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the suggestion type, which takes one input.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type, so what the input is stays unknown; GetName after other types (such as a trait's GetName with a character) is only a hint. The suggestion's key is localized as its name, per common/suggestions/_suggestions.info.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: An input the game does not document.

label: Suggestion type itself
summary: A function on a suggestion type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Accept contract
summary: The command to accept this task contract (a job an employer offers).
details: It gives a command, not an immediate action. Vanilla enables the button only when the command is valid and shows the command's reason as the tooltip when it is not.

label: Access contract itself
summary: A function on a task contract that, going by its name, hands back the contract itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Custom text
summary: Going by its name, a text from a custom localization entry, worked out for this task contract.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. On other types (such as Character.Custom('AIEconomicPersonality')) the input is the key of a custom localization entry; that is only a hint here.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the same function on other types, the key of the custom localization entry.

label: Completed reward text
summary: A text describing the reward of a completed task contract.
details: Vanilla shows it in the big event window, only when it is not empty. The content rests on its name and that use.

label: Contract destination
summary: Going by its name, the place the task contract sends its taker to.
details: Vanilla never uses it; texts use GetLocation for the place to travel to. The game documents no return type.

label: Employer
summary: The character who offers the task contract.
details: Vanilla's contract texts go on from it to the employer's top liege, primary title and title name, and compare it with the target's liege. The game documents no return type.

label: Contract location
summary: The place where the task contract is to be done.
details: Vanilla shows its name in contract texts, for example "This task contract requires you to travel to …". The game documents no return type.

label: Contract name
summary: The name of the task contract.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of contract icons on the main screen and on the map.

label: Contract name, plain
summary: The name of the task contract, without a tooltip of its own.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the shared tooltip templates (cooltip.gui), where a nested tooltip is not wanted.

label: Reward or failure text
summary: A text describing what happens when the task contract ends, for success or for failure.
details: Vanilla passes `'(bool)yes'` on the success tab and `'(bool)no'` on the failure tab of the task contract window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Yes for the success outcome, no for the failure outcome.

label: Full reward text
summary: A text that, going by its name, describes all the task contract's rewards.
details: Vanilla never uses it; GetRewardEffectDescription is the one vanilla shows.

label: Contract scheme
summary: Going by its name, the scheme (a plot over time) tied to the task contract.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetScheme('murder') and others are different uses and only a hint. HasScheme checks by name whether there is one. The game documents no return type.

label: Contractor
summary: The character who has taken the task contract.
details: Vanilla's contract name text checks whether this character is a landless adventurer, and the migration contract text uses their custom texts. The game documents no return type.

label: Contract target
summary: The target of the task contract, for example the ruler the employer is fed up with.
details: Vanilla's contract texts show the target's possessive name and compare its liege with the employer. What kind of target it is depends on the contract. The game documents no return type.

label: Contract description
summary: The description text of the task contract.
details: Vanilla shows it in the task contract window and in the contract's name tooltip.

label: Contract request
summary: The text saying what the task contract asks of its taker.
details: Vanilla shows it in the task contract window and in the contract's name tooltip. Contract request texts say, for example, that the contract requires travel to a place.

label: Contract tier
summary: A whole number that, going by its name, is the task contract's tier (its difficulty level).
details: Vanilla never uses it; the interface checks IsEasy, IsMedium and IsHard instead.

label: Contract type
summary: The task contract type (a definition in common/task_contracts) this contract is made from.
details: Vanilla goes on to the type's icon for contract icons on the main screen and on the map. The game documents no return type.

label: Has failure conditions
summary: Yes or no: whether the task contract has conditions under which it fails.
details: The task contract window shows a part only when this is yes, through TaskContractWindow.GetCurrentTaskContract.HasFailureConditions; the input lists that line as another type, but it leads to the current contract. The meaning rests on the name and that use.

label: Has scheme
summary: Yes or no that, going by its name, tells whether the task contract has a scheme tied to it.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Cancel contract
summary: The command to invalidate the task contract once it has been started.
details: It gives a command, not an immediate action. Vanilla shows the button only for a started contract, enables it only when the command is valid and asks for confirmation in a popup before carrying it out.

label: Is accepted
summary: Yes or no that, going by its name, tells whether the task contract has been accepted.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is completed
summary: Yes or no that, going by its name, tells whether the task contract has been completed.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Legend.IsCompleted and others are other types and only a hint.

label: Is criminal
summary: Yes or no: whether the task contract is a criminal one.
details: Vanilla combines it with the difficulty (IsEasy, IsMedium, IsHard) to pick which contract icon to show on the main screen and on the map.

label: Is easy
summary: Yes or no: whether the task contract is of the easy difficulty.
details: Vanilla combines it with IsCriminal to pick which contract icon to show on the main screen and on the map.

label: Is hard
summary: Yes or no: whether the task contract is of the hard difficulty.
details: Vanilla combines it with IsCriminal to pick which contract icon to show on the main screen and on the map.

label: Is in range
summary: Yes or no that, going by its name, tells whether the task contract is within reach.
details: Vanilla never uses it. What range is meant is not documented.

label: Is medium
summary: Yes or no: whether the task contract is of the medium difficulty.
details: Vanilla combines it with IsCriminal to pick which contract icon to show on the main screen and on the map.

label: Is opened
summary: Yes or no: whether the player has already opened (looked at) the task contract.
details: Vanilla shows a widget on the map icons only while this is no. That it marks unseen contracts rests on its name and that use.

label: Is valid
summary: Yes or no that, going by its name, tells whether this task contract exists.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. IsValid after other types (such as Character.GetGovernment.IsValid) checks that something is there; that is only a hint.

label: As script object
summary: The task contract as a script object, so texts can read its variables and script values.
details: It leads to a scope. Vanilla's contract texts go on with Var('task_contract_war') to read a variable stored on the contract.

label: Contract itself
summary: The task contract itself, to hand to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to ToggleGameViewData('task_contract', …) to open or close the task contract view when a contract icon is clicked. The game documents no return type.

label: Access contract type
summary: A function on a task contract type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Custom text
summary: Going by its name, a text from a custom localization entry, worked out for this task contract type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. On other types (such as Character.Custom('AIEconomicPersonality')) the input is the key of a custom localization entry; that is only a hint here.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the same function on other types, the key of the custom localization entry.
